title: Coupled SWRO Decision: Minimum Pressure and Acid-Dose Window
question_prompt:
Coupled SWRO Decision: Minimum Pressure and Acid-Dose Window

A coastal-well SWRO unit has operated for two years, and membrane water permeability is 20% below the new-membrane value. Operations require at least 0.380 kg/s permeate-water flow and no more than 350 ppm NaCl without adding membrane area, while preferring the lowest feasible feed pressure. After selecting pressure, pass the actual water recovery from simulate_ro into equilibrate_feed, check concentrate scaling, and identify the unique passing HCl dose from the discrete candidates. Recommend an executable pressure–acid setpoint.

reference_answer:
Gold Answer: 62 bar + 0.0022 mol/s HCl

Final recommendation: 62 bar feed pressure with 0.0022 mol/s HCl. This is the first pressure meeting both 0.38620 kg/s permeate-water flow and 328.35 ppm permeate NaCl; actual water recovery is 39.5623%. At that recovery, 0.0021 mol/s still fails with Dolomite SI=+0.00775, 0.0022 mol/s gives all four SIs below zero and pH=6.3139, while 0.0023 mol/s fails at pH=6.2838. The acid-dose window is therefore unique.

Model boundaries
simulate_ro represents salinity as NaCl equivalent, whereas equilibrate_feed uses the specified ions with a Pitzer activity model. The coupling variable is actual water recovery; the osmotic pressures need not match exactly. Equilibrium SI excludes nucleation/kinetics, antiscalant performance, fouling, acid mixing, degassing, corrosion, and control error. The 31 wt% acid conversion is an engineering estimate.
